heard: In 1957, astronomers logged a tiny, faint star that wasn't a star. Brallio Iraert and Enrique Chavira recorded entry 618 at Mexico's Tonnensintla Observatory as a white dwarf. In 1970, radio signals from Bologna and Spectra from McDonald Observatory revealed entry 618 was a quasar. Its central beacon shines with the brilliance of 140 trillion and suns, drowning out its host galaxy entirely. Infalling gas whirls around the core at speeds up to 10,500 kilometers per second, lighting up a nebula three times wider than the Milky Way. Depending on the spectral line analyzed, astronomers estimate its central black hole contains between 40.7 and 66 billion solar masses. from this ultra-massive engine traveled 10.8 billion years to reach Earth, where entry 618 looked like a tiny, faint star.
